selected_evidence.summary: Rules passed syntax validation. Before and after reboot, bounded 10-connection bursts produced 4 successes and 6 rate-limited failures with increasing nftables drop counters.
Authenticated SSH as arch succeeded through the firewall; final state shows sshd enabled, active, and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 22.
nftables and sshd are enabled. The same configuration hash and live IPv4/IPv6 rules were present before and after reboot.

Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from ab09f655-9d2b-4574-a072-db67e58266c2 to 8e946247-8dc1-4466-9572-f22fad56d61a; SSH and nftables recovered with authenticated access and live rules.
Temporary probe keys were removed. One managed administrator key remains, with correct ownership and permissions, and final authentication succeeded.

nftables v1.1.6 (Commodore Bullmoose #7)
iptables v1.8.13 (nf_tables)
#!/usr/bin/nft -f
# vim:set ts=2 sw=2 et:

# IPv4/IPv6 Simple & Safe firewall ruleset.
# More examples in /usr/share/nftables/ and /usr/share/doc/nftables/examples/.

destroy table inet filter
table inet filter {
  chain input {
    type filter hook input priority filter
    policy drop

    ct state invalid drop comment "early drop of invalid connections"
    ct state {established, related} accept comment "allow tracked connections"
    iif lo accept comment "allow from loopback"
    meta l4proto { icmp, icmpv6 } accept comment "allow icmp"
    tcp dport ssh accept comment "allow sshd"
    pkttype host limit rate 5/second counter reject with icmpx type admin-prohibited
    counter
  }
  chain forward {
    type filter hook forward priority filter
    policy drop
  }
}
# /usr/lib/systemd/system/nftables.service
[Unit]
Description=Netfilter Tables
Documentation=man:nft(8)
Wants=network-pre.target
Before=network-pre.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/nft -f /etc/nftables.conf

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
